import hashlib, json, sys, datetime, re, os
from pathlib import Path
proj, out, plugin = map(Path, sys.argv[1:4])
spec, tl = proj/"spec.md", proj/"proposed.md"
outr = out.resolve(strict=True)
for forbidden in [plugin/"skills", plugin/"agents", plugin/"commands", plugin/".claude-plugin"]:
    f = forbidden.resolve()
    assert not (outr == f or f in outr.parents or outr in f.parents), forbidden
for inp in [spec, tl, proj]:
    r = inp.resolve(strict=True)
    assert not (outr == r or outr in r.parents or r in outr.parents), inp
assert ".." not in out.parts
now = lambda: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
sha = lambda p: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
# link-follow depth 1: no file links in tasklist body
links = re.findall(r"\]\(([^)]+)\)", tl.read_text())
files = sorted([(str(p.relative_to(proj)), sha(p)) for p in [spec, tl]])
tree = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(files).encode()).hexdigest()
snap = {"input_tree_sha256": tree, "file_list": [{"path": a, "sha256": b} for a, b in files], "file_count": len(files),
        "linked_files_followed": links, "output_root_pinned": str(outr)}
(out/"artifacts"/"input-snapshot.yaml").write_text(json.dumps(snap, indent=2) + "\n")
rows = [
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.1","outcome":"ok","evidence_ref":None,"note":"flags parsed; --mode pre explicit (rule 1) -> UC-1; --tier 1 pin; --no-mcp; --no-promote"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.2","outcome":"ok","evidence_ref":None,"note":"spec.md and proposed.md exist, readable, non-empty"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.2b","outcome":"ok","evidence_ref":None,"note":"audit_repo_root="+str(proj)+" via git -C rev-parse --show-toplevel (git init only, no commits); selected inputs: spec.md, proposed.md; output pinned (component-checked: outside inputs, audit root, plugin dist dirs; no symlinks/..)"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.3","outcome":"skip","evidence_ref":None,"note":"sc-adversarial probe not needed: --tier 1 pinned, no Wave 4"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.4","outcome":"ok","evidence_ref":str(out/"artifacts"/"input-snapshot.yaml"),"note":"input_tree_sha256="+tree},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.5","outcome":"ok","evidence_ref":None,"note":"3 alias slots set, 3 distinct (values not printed); T2 not used due to --tier 1"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.5b","outcome":"warn","evidence_ref":None,"note":"executor class unresolved (no --executor-model/EXECUTOR_MODEL_CLASS/log); executor_class_source=unknown"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.5c","outcome":"skip","evidence_ref":None,"note":"--no-mcp: get_current_config not called; serena_version=unknown; degraded_components+=get_current_config"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.5d","outcome":"skip","evidence_ref":None,"note":"--no-mcp: backend=none, execute_shell_command_available=false, onboarding_available=false, read_only unconfirmed"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.5e","outcome":"skip","evidence_ref":None,"note":"native reviewer snapshot not provisioned: no Tier-2 reviewers (--tier 1)"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.6","outcome":"warn","evidence_ref":None,"note":"vendor heuristic: 2 slots anthropic-named, 1 slot non-anthropic-named -> multi (heuristic, warn-only, unused at T1)"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.7","outcome":"skip","evidence_ref":None,"note":"--no-mcp: no Serena activation/memory; onboarding_status=unknown"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.7b","outcome":"skip","evidence_ref":None,"note":"--onboard not set"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.8","outcome":"ok","evidence_ref":str(out/"audit.log"),"note":"audit log opened"},
 {"wave":0,"step":"0.9","outcome":"skip","evidence_ref":None,"note":"--budget-remaining unset; budget_check_skipped=true"},
]
with open(out/"audit.log","w") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps({"header":"sc:sc-reflect audit log","contract_version":"1.8.0","mode":"pre","audit_repo_root":str(proj),"output_root":str(outr),"plugin_root":str(plugin),"selected_inputs":[str(spec),str(tl)]})+"\n")
    for r in rows: r["timestamp"]=now(); f.write(json.dumps(r)+"\n")
# Pass 1 deterministic extraction + exact matching
ID = re.compile(r"\b(R-\d+|REQ-\d+|SPEC-\d+|T-\d+)\b")
def ids(text):
    out=[]; fence=False
    for i,l in enumerate(text.splitlines(),1):
        if l.strip().startswith("```"): fence=not fence; continue
        if fence: continue
        for m in ID.findall(l): out.append((m,i,l))
    return out
spec_ids=[(m,i,l) for m,i,l in ids(spec.read_text()) if not m.startswith("T-")]
tasks={}; cur=None
for i,l in enumerate(tl.read_text().splitlines(),1):
    m=re.match(r"^#+\s+(T-\d+)",l)
    if m: cur=m.group(1); tasks[cur]={"line":i,"text":l}
    elif cur: tasks[cur]["text"]+="\n"+l
matrix=[]
for rid,line,_ in spec_ids:
    matched=sorted(t for t,v in tasks.items() if re.search(r"\b"+re.escape(rid)+r"\b",v["text"]))
    matrix.append({"requirement_id":rid,"spec_line":line,"source":"parsed","matched_task_ids":matched,"match_method":"exact" if matched else "none"})
(out/"artifacts"/"coverage-pass1.json").write_text(json.dumps({"total_tasks":len(tasks),"tasks":{k:v["line"] for k,v in tasks.items()},"matrix":matrix},indent=2)+"\n")
print(json.dumps({"tree":tree,"tasks":len(tasks),"matrix":matrix}))
EOF

# Wave 1C Tier-1 reflection card — persisted verbatim by orchestrator from sc:sc-root-cause-analyst
# requested_model_slot: sonnet ; agent self-reported model: claude-sonnet-5-5[1m] ; agentId: aa3afd307f3c73fdf

# Orchestrator note: S_domains: card infers 2 (code, tests) [INFERRED]; orchestrator counted 1 from the input paths (docs). Not load-bearing: --tier 1 pinned.
card_id: t1-card
mode: pre
author_agent: sc:sc-root-cause-analyst
author_model_self_reported: Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5[1m])
inputs: [spec.md, proposed.md]
coverage_summary:
  coverage_pct: 1.00
  parsed: 3   # R-001, R-002, R-003 (spec.md:5, :8, :11), each mapped to exactly one task (proposed.md:3, :6, :9)
  inferred: 0
  unmapped: []
  notes: >
    Mapping is by explicit R-id in the proposed.md task headings, so no inference was needed.
    S_scope = 3 tasklist items. S_domains = 2 (code and tests) [INFERRED, because neither file names paths].
    S_dev_density = 0/3 = 0.00.
    The orchestrator's artifacts/coverage-matrix.yaml was NOT found at the stated path (Read returned "File does not exist"),
    so the matrix was not used as evidence. Coverage here is my own mapping from spec.md and proposed.md.
    Coverage is structural. T-101 is only loosely tied to the exact-string requirement (see F-3).
findings:
  - id: F-1
    claim: >
      Every spec requirement has a one-to-one task. R-001 maps to T-101, R-002 to T-102, R-003 to T-103.
      No spec requirement is missing a task, and no task lacks a spec requirement.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:5, spec.md:8, spec.md:11, proposed.md:3, proposed.md:6, proposed.md:9]
    severity: low
  - id: F-2
    claim: >
      T-102 restates the R-002 behavior faithfully. Both say an empty name is rejected with ValueError.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:9, proposed.md:7]
    severity: low
  - id: F-3
    claim: >
      T-101 says "returning the required greeting" and never states the exact literal "Hello, Ada!" from R-001.
      An implementer could hard-code the Ada case, or pick a different template for other names.
      The task gives no acceptance string, so its fidelity to the MUST is unverifiable from the plan alone.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:6, proposed.md:4]
    severity: medium
  - id: F-4
    claim: >
      R-001 pins the output only for the input Ada. The generic format ("Hello, <name>!") is implied but not specified,
      and the plan does not resolve the ambiguity.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:6, proposed.md:4]
    severity: low
  - id: F-5
    claim: >
      T-103 requires "ordinary and empty-name test cases", which matches the R-003 wording. It does not require the tests to assert
      the exact string "Hello, Ada!" or to assert the ValueError type (for example with pytest.raises(ValueError)).
      A test that only checks "no crash" or "some exception" would satisfy the task text.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:12, proposed.md:10]
    severity: medium
  - id: F-6
    claim: >
      The plan names no target file, module, or test path, and has no verification command, acceptance criteria, or task ordering.
      The spec likewise names no module or signature beyond "greet function", so the plan cannot be checked for placement or run.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [proposed.md:1-10, spec.md:1-12]
    severity: medium
  - id: F-7
    claim: >
      Edge cases are unaddressed by both spec and plan. "Empty" is not defined, so whitespace-only input is open.
      Non-string or None input is also open. The plan does not decide these, which leaves room for divergent implementations.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:9, proposed.md:7]
    severity: low
  - id: F-8
    claim: >
      No requirement carries a durable_sink or @sink annotation, so the contracted-sink reachability ledger is not applicable.
    tag: INFERRED
    citations: [spec.md:1-12]
    severity: low
plan_vs_spec_deviations: []   # none: no task contradicts or expands its requirement. The gaps are under-specification, not divergence.
risks:
  - id: K-1
    risk: >
      Hard-coded or under-generalized greeting. T-101 lacks the exact-string acceptance, so a weak implementation could pass a
      loose reading of the task while missing R-001.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:6, proposed.md:4]
  - id: K-2
    risk: >
      Weak tests give false assurance for R-002 and R-003. Without a pinned exception type and expected string, the tests may not
      protect R-001 and R-002 against later regression.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:9, spec.md:12, proposed.md:10]
  - id: K-3
    risk: >
      Unspecified empty-input semantics (whitespace, None) may lead to inconsistent behavior or a post-hoc dispute during the
      later audit.
    tag: INFERRED
    citations: [spec.md:9, proposed.md:7]
  - id: K-4
    risk: >
      With no file targets or run command, execution evidence may not be reproducible. A later UC-2 audit would have trouble
      confirming that the tests ran and passed.
    tag: INFERRED
    citations: [proposed.md:1-10]
  - id: K-5
    risk: >
      Blast radius is minimal. Three small tasks on a synthetic fixture have no cross-module impact, and no regression candidates
      exist because no prior code is in scope.
    tag: grounded
    citations: [spec.md:3, proposed.md:1-10]
best_practice_grade: >
  3/5. Strengths: complete one-to-one traceability with explicit R-ids, no scope creep, and a test task that matches R-003 (F-1, F-2).
  Weaknesses: no exact acceptance literal (F-3), no assertion-level test requirements (F-5), and no file targets,
  verifier commands, or ordering (F-6). The plan is adequate in coverage but thin in verifiability.
recommendations:
  - id: R-1
    file: proposed.md (T-101, line 4)
    change: >
      Reword to say greet("Ada") must return exactly "Hello, Ada!". State the general template (for example "Hello, <name>!").
      Name the target module and function signature.
    verifier: >
      After execution, a test asserts greet("Ada") == "Hello, Ada!". A grep of the module and tests shows the literal, and a
      pytest run exits 0.
    priority: P1
    linked_findings: [F-3, F-4, F-6]
  - id: R-2
    file: proposed.md (T-103, line 10)
    change: >
      Require tests that (a) assert equality with "Hello, Ada!" and (b) use pytest.raises(ValueError) on greet(""). Name the test file path.
    verifier: >
      pytest -q on that file passes. Mutating the greeting string or the exception type makes a test fail.
    priority: P1
    linked_findings: [F-5, F-6]
  - id: R-3
    file: proposed.md (T-102, line 7)
    change: >
      Decide and state whether whitespace-only and None inputs are in scope. If not, add a one-line "out of scope" note;
      if so, add a matching spec clause and test.
    verifier: >
      proposed.md contains an explicit statement on the edge cases. If they are in scope, the tests cover them and pass.
    priority: P2
    linked_findings: [F-7]
